51443657.DESCRIPTION: Inhibition of TAM-3Y-F2Pmp peptide binding to N-terminal His6-fused STEP32 (282 to 563 residues) (unknown origin) expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Measurement of B: For the interaction studies, the immobilized peptides were used as ligands, while the catalytically inactive mutant form, STEP32 C/S, was used for the interaction with p3Y and p-fin4 phosphopeptides, while the catalytically active form STEP32 WT was used for the interaction with F2Pmp-containing peptides. The initial concentration of the STEP32 protein was estimated using the Pierce 660nm Protein Assay Reagent (Thermo) and the FLUOStar Omega Microplate Reader (BMG LABTECH). For each kinetic experiment, a series of at least five different concentrations of STEP32, ranging between 50 nM and 500 μM, were injected onto each peptide immobilized on the sensor chip, at a flow rate of 10 μL/min, in a random order. STEP32 concentrations were prepared as serial dilutions in HBS-EP buffer (0.01 M HEPES pH 7.4, 0.15 M NaCl, 3 mM EDTA, 2 mM DTT, 0.005% v/v Surfactant P20). The association and dissociation time was set to 5 min. After each kinetic test, 2–4 cycles of regeneration were performed by injecting 1 M NaCl in HBS-EP buffer for 2 min at a flow rate of 20 μL/min. All binding measurements were carried out at 25 °C with HBS-EP as the running buffer. For p3Y, 3Y-F2Pmp, and 3Ysh-3-F2Pmp, the experiments were performed in duplicate and each STEP32 dilution was injected two times. In the case of the p-fin4 peptide, one binding experiment was performed and all STEP32 C/S dilutions were injected in duplicate. Nonspecific bindings were removed by separately subtracting the signal registered on the reference cell from the signal registered on each peptide-immobilized cell surface. The dissociation constant Kd values were calculated using GraphPad Prism 6.0 software by fitting the data to the regression-one-site specific binding model. All sensorgrams and steady-state plots shown in this manuscript as well as in the Supporting Information were prepared using Prism 6.0 (GraphPad Software).
